title: Samplers and Sampling Strategies
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of samplers and sampling strategies in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of samplers and sampling strategies and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Samplers and Sampling Strategies: A Dataset describes how to retrieve one sample, while a DataLoader groups samples into batches and controls ordering, worker processes, and collation. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: A dependable data pipeline makes training repeatable and prevents shape, label, leakage, and throughput problems from being mistaken for model problems. For this lesson, focus on sequential sampling and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep sample retrieval separate from batching and transforms. Split data before fitting preprocessing, and ensure train/validation/inference transformations are appropriate to each stage. The source topics for this lesson are: Sequential sampling, Random sampling, Weighted sampling. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.text: Inspect one dataset item, one batched output, and the feature/label shapes. Use num_workers=0 while debugging custom datasets. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
from torch.utils.data import WeightedRandomSampler
weights = [1.0, 1.0, 5.0]
sampler = WeightedRandomSampler(weights, num_samples=4, replacement=True)
print(len(list(sampler)))

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not shuffle or split features and labels independently; their indices must remain aligned.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
